anatomy.flutter: Card(children: [...]) containing an ordered list of CardHeader(title, description, action), CardContent(child), CardFooter(child) widgets, with CardHeader building CardTitle + optional CardDescription in a Column and an optional CardAction in a Row beside it.
anatomy.web: Card > CardHeader (grid, containing CardTitle, optional CardDescription, optional CardAction as col-start-2) > CardContent (px-(--card-spacing)) > CardFooter (flex items-center border-t bg-muted/50), each stamped with its own data-slot attribute.

api.flutter: Card({children, fill, ringColor}); CardTitle(String text); CardDescription(String text); no `size`/`sm` variant at all -- the doc comment says so explicitly ('Not ported: data-size="sm" (no card in the corpus passes it)').
api.web: Card({className, size = "default" | "sm", ...props}) -- size="sm" shrinks --card-spacing to space(3) via data-[size=sm]:[--card-spacing:--spacing(3)] and CardTitle reads group-data-[size=sm]/card:text-sm.
api.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The web's `size` prop (default|sm) is a real, working API surface (Card.tsx line 8-16, CardTitle.tsx line 56) that has no Flutter equivalent whatsoever -- Card and CardTitle in Dart take no size parameter. The Flutter doc comment frames this as an intentional 'not ported' decision because no current call site uses it, but as an API-parity question this is a gap: a caller wanting the small-card density has nothing to reach for on the Flutter side.

states.flutter: Card is a StatelessWidget with no built-in interaction state; only fill/ringColor are exposed as overridable colours for a caller's own hover wiring (doc comment: 'the stat page's navigating card hovers to bg-accent... hovers to ring-action/45').
states.web: Card itself renders no interactive pseudo-classes of its own; any hover/focus state is applied by the page around it.
states.note: Neither side gives Card an intrinsic interaction state matrix -- it is a passive container in both systems, so this dimension does not apply to the component itself.

disabled.flutter: No disabled concept exists on Card, CardHeader, CardContent, or CardFooter.
disabled.web: No disabled prop or data-disabled hook exists on Card or any of its sub-parts.
disabled.note: Card is a layout/surface primitive, not a control; a disabled state does not apply to either implementation.

interaction.flutter: Card exposes no pointer, keyboard or focus handling of its own; it is pure layout and paint (DecoratedBox + ClipRRect + Padding + Column).
interaction.web: Card renders a plain <div data-slot="card">; interaction is entirely delegated to whatever the caller puts inside it.
interaction.note: As a container rather than a control, Card carries no interaction contract on either platform.

semantics.flutter: CardTitle always renders as StyledText(text, TextStyles.h4) -- a plain text widget with no heading-level semantics; there is no asChild-equivalent or documented way to make the title announce as an actual heading.
semantics.web: CardTitle accepts asChild (via Slot.Root) specifically so a caller can render the title as an <h2>/<h3>/etc rather than a <div>, with the doc comment explaining why: 'a page of cards whose titles are all <div>s is a page with no headings in it: nothing to navigate by, and no outline.'

This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. ORIGINAL: This is a real accessibility-surfaced gap: the web's CardTitle asChild pattern is the documented mechanism for giving a card page a real heading outline for screen-reader/AT navigation, and the Flutter CardTitle has no equivalent hook (no Semantics(header: true) option, no way to vary the rendered role). A Flutter screen composing many cards has no way to reproduce the same navigable heading outline the web achieves.
